links.outcome: Adenoma detection rate with versus without CADe in real-world colonoscopy, by procedure order
links.effect: CADe ADR 49.9% in first 3 procedures vs 39.4% unassisted; later procedures 39.9% vs 40.9%, so the benefit disappeared later in the day.
links.quote: CADe assistance significantly improved ADR during early-day colonoscopies, but this benefit disappeared in later-day procedures.

links.outcome: Clinician performance with AI in real workflow versus without, across the day
links.effect: Adenomas per colonoscopy rose +0.27 (95% CI 0.14-0.41) early with CADe but only +0.11 (95% CI -0.09 to 0.31, P=0.51) later.
links.quote: Similarly, adenomas per colonoscopy were significantly higher in early CADe-assisted procedures (mean increase +0.27, 95% CI [0.14-0.41], P < 0.001), but this benefit disappeared in later procedures (+0.11, 95% CI [-0.09 to 0.31], P = 0.51).

links.outcome: Performance of endoscopists with versus without AI in deployment, assessing reliance/fatigue
links.effect: Early CADe ADR 49.9% vs 39.4% unassisted; late CADe ADR 39.9% vs 40.9% unassisted, suggesting diminished responsiveness to CADe.
links.quote: By contrast, ADR in CADe-assisted procedures was markedly higher in the first 3 procedures (49.9%, 95% CI [45.5-54.3]) but dropped significantly to 39.9% (95% CI [33.8-46.3]) in later procedures.

links.outcome: Alert fatigue reducing CADe effectiveness through the day
links.effect: CADe-assisted ADR fell from 49.9% in first 3 procedures to 39.9% in later procedures; ADR gain per WT minute 10.5% early vs 10.1% late.
links.quote: This pattern suggests that alert fatigue may limit endoscopists' responsiveness to CADe prompts as the day progresses.

screen.reason: The study empirically evaluates real-world clinical implementation and alert fatigue over time during CADe colonoscopy, but it evaluates the overall performance drop across procedure order rather than comparing specific deployment practices or safeguards.
